title: Accounts Assistant
description:
Accounts Assistant

Cosgrove & Cosgrove Ltd Telford, Shropshire

£28,000-£30,000 per annum depending on experience Full-time Permanent Office-based

Cosgrove & Cosgrove is looking for an experienced Accounts Assistant to join our small finance team in Telford, supporting the day-to-day accounts across multiple businesses.

This is a hands-on role for someone who enjoys keeping accurate records, resolving queries and taking ownership of their work. You should be confident completing bank reconciliations independently and managing a varied workload without constant supervision.

What you'll be doing
- Completing bank reconciliations independently across multiple accounts and investigating discrepancies.
- Maintaining purchase and sales ledgers, processing supplier invoices, and raising and processing sales invoices.
- Processing expenses and credit card transactions, matching receipts and following up missing information.
- Using Dext to support invoice and receipt processing.
- Carrying out bookkeeping and data entry, keeping QuickBooks Online records accurate and up to date.
- Preparing and posting journals, including payroll journals, and collating payroll information.
- Liaising with colleagues and suppliers to resolve queries.
- Supporting month-end tasks and the wider finance team.

What we're looking for
- At least two years' practical UK accounts or bookkeeping experience.
- The ability to complete bank reconciliations independently.
- Practical experience of purchase and sales ledgers, supplier invoices and expenses.
- Good Excel skills and practical experience using QuickBooks Online. Both are essential.
- Strong attention to detail, good organisation and the ability to prioritise your workload.
- A reliable commute to our Telford office for this fully office-based role.

Experience using Dext would be an advantage. An AAT qualification or progress towards one would be useful, but is not essential; practical experience and the ability to do the work are what matter.

How to apply

Please submit your CV and include a short covering note answering the following:
- How many years of practical UK accounts or bookkeeping experience do you have?
- How many years have you used QuickBooks Online, and have you used Dext?
- What experience do you have of preparing payroll information and posting payroll journals?
- How would you describe your Excel level? Please give examples of the functions or tasks you use regularly.
- What are you looking for in your next role and why are you leaving your current position? If you are not currently employed, please tell us what you are looking for next.
- What is your notice period or earliest available start date?

title: Accounts Payable Clerk
description:
Salary: £26,500 - £28,000 (depending on experience)
Location: Albrighton, fully office-based
Job Type: Full-Time, Permanent

We are seeking an experienced Accounts Payable Clerk to join a busy and collaborative finance function. This is an excellent opportunity for a finance professional who enjoys working in a fast-paced environment, building strong supplier relationships and ensuring the accurate processing of financial transactions.

Working as part of a supportive team, you will play a key role in maintaining the purchase ledger, managing supplier accounts and helping to ensure the smooth operation of day-to-day finance activities.

The Role

This position will suit someone who thrives in a detail-focused role and takes pride in delivering accurate work while meeting deadlines.

Key Responsibilities
- Manage the end-to-end processing of supplier invoices, ensuring accuracy and timely posting.
- Maintain supplier accounts, investigate discrepancies and resolve queries efficiently.
- Reconcile statements and ensure outstanding items are addressed promptly.
- Assist with scheduled payment runs and support cashflow management activities.
- Build positive working relationships with suppliers and internal stakeholders.
- Support month-end activities and contribute to accurate financial reporting.
- Ensure financial records are maintained to a high standard and in line with company procedures.
- Provide general support across the finance department as required.

About You

We're looking for someone who combines strong transactional finance experience with excellent attention to detail and a proactive approach.

Ideally, you will have:
- Experience within Accounts Payable or a similar finance position.
- Good Excel skills and confidence working with financial data.
- Experience using finance or accounting systems.
- A methodical approach with excellent levels of accuracy.
- Strong organisational skills and the ability to manage multiple priorities.
- Excellent communication skills and a customer-focused mindset.
- The ability to work independently and as part of a wider team.

Apply Now

If you're an experienced Accounts Payable professional looking to join a successful and growing business where your contribution will be valued, we'd love to hear from you. Apply today with your CV.

title: Credit Control
description:
The Role

We are looking for an experienced and proactive Credit Controller to join a busy finance team, This is a key role within the business, responsible for managing the full credit control function and ensuring the timely collection of outstanding debt across a varied ledger.

You will be a confident communicator who is comfortable building relationships with clients while maintaining firm control over outstanding balances. You will bring a methodical approach to your work, a strong eye for detail, and the ability to manage a high-volume workload without losing sight of the bigger picture.

Please note: This role is exclusively recruited for via Consula. Applications made outside of Consula will not be considered and cannot progress. To apply, you must submit your application through the Consula platform

Key Responsibilities

Manage a busy ledger, proactively chasing outstanding invoices by telephone, email, and letter in line with agreed credit terms.

Build and maintain strong relationships with clients, resolving payment queries and disputes efficiently and professionally.

Monitor debtor accounts and escalate overdue balances in line with company policy.

Allocate cash receipts accurately and reconcile accounts on a regular basis.

Prepare aged debtor reports and present updates to the finance team and senior management.

Liaise with internal teams including sales, operations, and customer service to resolve billing queries and disputes.

Assess the creditworthiness of new and existing customers, recommending credit limits where appropriate.

Support the wider finance team with month-end processes and reporting as required.

What We Are Looking For

Proven experience in a Credit Control role, with a track record of successfully reducing debtor days and managing a high-volume ledger.

Strong communication skills - you are confident on the telephone and in writing, and can handle difficult conversations professionally and calmly.

Highly organised, with the ability to prioritise a busy workload and meet deadlines consistently.

Proficient in accounting software and Microsoft Excel.

A team player who is also capable of working independently and using their own initiative.

What's On Offer

Hybrid working with flexibility built in.

A stable, permanent role within a well-established business.

Supportive finance team with real opportunities to develop your career.

Competitive benefits package including pension and holiday allowance.

This organisation is recruiting directly through Consula, their recruitment partner.

title: Payroll Administrator
description:
Hours of Work: Monday-Friday: 08:30-17:00

About the Role

We are looking for a highly organised and detail-oriented Data Administrator to join our clients Payroll team. This is an excellent opportunity for an experienced administrator who enjoys working with data and has a keen eye for accuracy.

You will be responsible for maintaining employee records, inputting payroll-related data, and providing administrative support across various payroll and fleet administration activities. This role offers a fantastic opportunity to learn, develop, and build a career within payroll.

Key Responsibilities
- Accurately input and maintain payroll-related data and figures.
- Record and monitor employee absences, ensuring information is accurate and matches payroll records.
- Manage and organise payroll email inboxes, responding to queries and directing communications appropriately.
- File and maintain electronic documents using Microsoft Office applications.
- Support fleet administration activities, including organising and managing fuel cards.
- Ensure payroll records and administration processes are maintained accurately and confidentially.
- Assist with general administrative duties to support the Payroll Team.
- Communicate professionally with employees and stakeholders via telephone and email.

Skills & Experience Required
- Previous administration experience.
- Excellent attention to detail and accuracy.
- Strong organisational and time management skills.
- Analytical mindset with the ability to work confidently with numerical data.
- Good Excel skills and confidence working with Microsoft Office applications.
- Ability to manage multiple tasks and priorities effectively.
- Professional and confident telephone manner.
- Strong communication and interpersonal skills.
- Ability to work independently as well as part of a team.

What We Offer
- Opportunity to learn and develop within a professional Payroll Team.
- Supportive working environment with ongoing training.
- Valuable exposure to payroll processes and systems.
- Career development opportunities.
- Access to employee well-being scheme

If you are a proactive administrator who enjoys working with data, has excellent organisational skills, and is looking for an opportunity to develop within payroll, we would love to hear from you.

title: Payroll Assistant
description:
We are looking for experienced and proactive Payroll Assistants to join our clients payroll team on a temporary basis, starting immediately. This is a busy, hands-on role for someone with a strong payroll background who can hit the ground running.

Key Responsibilities:
- Processing payroll input and administration tasks
- Supporting payroll data entry and validation activities
- Assisting with employee payroll amendments, starters, leavers and contractual changes
- Reviewing and investigating payroll exceptions and anomalies
- Supporting pension administration and payroll-related deductions
- Validating employee expenses and payroll adjustments
- Responding to routine payroll queries from employees and stakeholders
- Assisting with payroll reconciliations and maintaining accurate payroll records
- Supporting statutory and compliance-related payroll activities where required
- Working under the direction of the Payroll Manager and wider Payroll team

Skills & Experience Required:
- Strong, recent experience in a payroll role, with a solid understanding of end-to-end payroll processing
- Working knowledge of statutory payroll requirements, pensions and payroll deductions
- Experience of handling starters, leavers, amendments and payroll exceptions accurately
- Confident using Microsoft Excel and payroll systems
- High attention to detail with the ability to manage a busy and varied workload
- Strong communicator with a professional approach to handling confidential information
- Well-organised, self-motivated, and able to work independently as well as part of a team

If you are a motivated payroll professional looking for a varied short-term role within a busy, friendly team, and are available to start straight away, we would love to hear from you.
